subject: POC Kickoff: Load testing & benchmarking session - scheduling
messages:
From: Alex Brown <alex.brown@greengrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: POC kickoff and load testing benchmarks

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood last week. We are excited to get the POC kicked off. The primary objectives for our team are to validate throughput and latency for our routing and prompt set, and to run an initial load test against a realistic traffic profile. High level targets we want to verify during the POC:
- Throughput: 500 req/s sustained for 60 minutes
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for generation requests at 2k token context
- Verify routing fallbacks and KV cache behavior under mixed traffic

Can we schedule a 90 minute hands-on working session the week of June 14 to review prompts, routing rules, and run the initial load test? Ideally it would include your engineering team to pair on the harness.

Our primary engineers who will join are Paul Singh (paul.singh@datacorp.com) and myself. Let me know availability windows and any pre-reqs we should prepare.

Thanks,
Alex Brown
Head of Platform Engineering
GreenGrid

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Brown <alex.brown@greengrid.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and load testing benchmarks

Hi Alex,

Great to hear — we can definitely get that scheduled. Dev (cc) will lead the load test run and review the harness with your team. Proposed windows (all PT):
- Tue Jun 15: 10:00-11:30 or 15:00-16:30
- Wed Jun 16: 09:00-10:30 or 14:00-15:30

We typically do a 30-45 minute prompt/routing walkthrough followed by a 45-60 minute load run. I attached a short kickoff agenda and our runbook for the test steps. Pre-reqs we need from you:
- Temporary IP allowlist for our test runners (we can provide CIDR)
- A representative prompt set and sample traffic mix (ratios of chat vs. high-latency generation)
- Confirmation on the dataset size you want to use for KV/cache tests

Does any of the proposed windows work for you and Paul? If so, we will send a calendar invite and include the harness repo link and a doc with the workload config.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: poc-agenda.pdf, redwood-runbook.pdf

From: Alex Brown <alex.brown@greengrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Singh <paul.singh@datacorp.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and load testing benchmarks

Thanks Marissa — Tue Jun 15 15:00-16:30 PT works best for our team. Paul and I can join that slot.

A couple of asks before the session:
- Can you share the harness repo and an example workload config so Paul can review ahead of time?
- For the allowlist, please send the CIDR blocks and approximate egress IPs.
- For the KV/cache tests, we plan to exercise a 1M-key dataset; is that feasible for the POC environment?

We will also record the session. Looking forward to pairing on this.

Alex

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Brown <alex.brown@greengrid.com>, Paul Singh <paul.singh@datacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and load testing benchmarks

Hi Alex / Paul,

Quick technical pre-reqs and notes before we run the load:
- IP allowlist: we will provide two CIDR ranges for our runners: 35.199.32.0/19 and 34.82.0.0/16. Please open outbound to our endpoints on port 443.
- Auth: we will provision a short-lived API key scoped to the POC project; please confirm the email to tie to the key audit logs.
- KV/cache dataset: 1M keys is OK for an initial run but we recommend starting at 200k and stepping up to 1M over 3 phases to avoid noisy degradation.
- Harness: we attached the load-test-harness-spec.md with the workload template and example command lines. The harness uses a statsd sink and pushes p50/p95/p99 to the shared dashboard.

Plan for the session (15 Jun 15:00 PT):
1) 15:00-15:30 — prompt review, routing rules, and expected fallbacks
2) 15:30-16:15 — stepped load run (200k -> 500k -> 1M keys)
3) 16:15-16:30 — wrap and next steps (tuning, extended runs)

Please confirm the contact for API key audit tie and whether you want us to provision a temporary VPC peering instead of public allowlist.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: load-test-harness-spec.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Brown <alex.brown@greengrid.com>, Paul Singh <paul.singh@datacorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and load testing benchmarks

Hi Alex,

Heads up — an internal conflict came up for some of our infra engineers on Jun 15 morning. Can we move the hands-on session to Tue Jun 16 15:00-16:30 PT instead? Same agenda, just shifted by one day. If that does not work for you, we can keep Jun 15 15:00 and have two Redwood engineers on the call, but we prefer Jun 16 to have the primary owner.

I will send the calendar invite once you confirm. I attached an updated kickoff agenda referencing the phased load plan. Timezones noted: 15:00-16:30 PT / 18:00-19:30 ET.

Apologies for the shuffle and thanks for the flexibility.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: poc-agenda.pdf

From: Alex Brown <alex.brown@greengrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Singh <paul.singh@datacorp.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff and load testing benchmarks

Thanks Marissa — Tue Jun 16 15:00-16:30 PT works for us. Paul and I will be there. Please include the harness repo link and the example workload config in the invite so Paul can spin up a local dry run before we pair.

For the API key audit tie, use paul.singh@datacorp.com as the contact. We prefer allowlist for this first run; we can discuss VPC peering later.

See you on the 16th.

Alex
